title: From Representation to Readout: Mechanistic Analysis of Membership Signals in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.41445v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Membership inference aims to determine whether a particular example was included in a model's training data. Such membership signals are often broadly described as memorization, while the underlying mechanisms can involve both how information is represented internally and how it is accessed by the model to produce behaviors. We therefore present a mechanistic study of membership signals in large language models (LLMs). We introduce Decodable Information Score, Used Information Score, and Readout Accessibility Gap (DUG), a set of complementary measures that separately quantify membership information decodable from internal representations and the extent to which it is exposed through the model's readout. Across supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL)-based membership inference methods, membership-specific effects appear in both the amount of decodable information and readout under SFT, while under RL-based membership

translated_title: 从表征到读取：语言模型中成员信号的机制分析
translated_abstract: 成员推断旨在判断某个特定样本是否被包含在模型的训练数据中。这类成员信号通常被笼统地描述为“记忆”，而其潜在机制既可能涉及信息在模型内部的表征方式，也可能涉及模型为产生行为而对信息进行访问的方式。因此，我们对大语言模型（LLM）中的成员信号开展了机制层面的研究。我们提出了可解码信息分数、已使用信息分数和读取可及性差距，这是一组互补的度量指标，可以分别量化从内部表征中可解码出的成员信息量，以及这些信息通过模型读取过程被暴露出来的程度。在基于监督微调（SFT）和基于强化学习（RL）的成员推断方法中，研究发现：在SFT下，成员特定效应同时体现在可解码信息量和读取过程两个层面，而在基于RL的成员（推断中，摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出DUG（可解码信息分数、已使用信息分数、读取可及性差距）三种互补度量，首次从机制层面将大语言模型成员推断信号分解为内部表征中的可解码信息与读取过程暴露程度两个独立维度，并分析了SFT与RL训练方式下成员效应的分布差异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DUG (Decodable Information Score, Used Information Score, and Readout Accessibility Gap), a set of complementary measures that mechanistically disentangle membership signals in LLMs into information decodable from internal representations versus information exposed through model readout, revealing how membership-specific effects differ under SFT- and RL-based training.
